_method_version: 2.0.0 is a MAJOR bump and revises the 1.x headline twice over. 1.x ran on a systematic 1-in-3 sample of 1,459 decisions and reported that two articles were 41% of enforced citations. On the full population of 3,361 the same measure is 35%, the tail is 53 articles rather than 22, and Article 32 doubles from 10% to 20% of decisions — the sample materially overstated concentration. 1.x also asserted that GDPRhub carries no fine amount and that Party_Name is empty; both are wrong, 71% of decisions carry a fine and 63% name a party. Rows written under 1.x are not comparable and are kept, not deleted. 2.1.0 adds two controls that were open questions: the Article 6 premium survives holding authority and case type fixed, and the slowdown survives a fixed authority panel (+72%, against +41% unadjusted).

source.name: GDPRhub
source._pages_enumerated: Page list enumerated 2026-09-07; content fetched 2026-09-09/10. 3,510 of these pages are not decisions (categories, templates, help) and parse to nothing.

corpus._note: Not committed. Reproduce with fetch-gdprhub.py; the wiki is edited continuously, so a later fetch will differ.

compound._what: median euro fine when an article is cited alone, versus with two or more others

fixed_panel._what: authorities with dated decisions in every year of the window

art6_premium_controlled._what: single-article decisions, Spain, complaint type only — controls authority and case type

not_answerable.company_killing: GDPRhub records no revenue, employee count or company identifier, so severity relative to the company cannot be measured and the 4%-of-turnover cap cannot be checked.
not_answerable.appeal_rate: Only 12% of decisions record a real Appeal_To_Status; the rest are blank or Unknown.
not_answerable.what_is_not_prosecuted: The corpus is decisions authorities chose to publish. Cases that closed quietly are invisible, so non-enforcement cannot be read off it.
